StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The over-organized class rep who tracks every itinerary change with her battered clipboard

NodeText.Line: *The class rep glances up from her clipboard*
You look like you can handle things. We really need help.
Dark spirits are messing up the shrine paths. Everyone's stuck.
Any luck with the spirits? Everyone's getting worried.
You did it! The paths are clear again. We all owe you.
Hey, I remember you from before. Still handling the trouble.
Their leader calls herself the Rival Chief. She's pulled the troublemakers together.
They block paths, corner students, and scare off the tour groups.
There's a school bounty on the Chief, two hundred credits.
Keep anything you find in their spot. They've taken enough already.
Their spot is somewhere past the outer grounds, but we don't know exactly.
If you deal with the lookouts on the paths, one might drop a map.
We count at least a dozen, maybe more. Lookouts patrol the paths.
The Chief has a few tough followers who do the rough work.
Thanks so much. Watch yourself out there, they're tougher than they look.
Okay. If you change your mind, come back. People need help.
Nice! Every one you stop weakens their group.
Keep going. Once you find their spot, move fast.
Please hurry. Another group got blocked just yesterday.
Is that... the Chief's badge? You really did it!
This calls for a group cheer! The paths are safe again.
Of course! You've earned every bit.
The bounty is yours. The whole class is grateful.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A rival student posted on the path to warn others away

NodeText.Line: Stop right there. Empty your bag and you can keep going.
*The lookout's eyes go wide*
Wait! Don't come closer! Here, take this map to their spot.
Just let me pass, okay?
Big talk. You'll regret it. Get them!
You're going to wish you stayed back!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A tall student who uses his size to block anyone the Chief dislikes

NodeText.Line: *A broad-shouldered student steps out, rolling his shoulders*
That's far enough. The Chief doesn't want visitors.
Then you'll stay right here!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The pushy leader of a rival group trying to take over the shrine visit

NodeText.Line: *The rival leader stands up from the stone bench, hand on her bag*
So the class finally sent someone worth facing. Come on then.
Let's see what you've got!
So you're the one who's been messing with my group.
I've handled plenty like you. You'll be next.
Not bad. Better than the usual tour kids.
Skill won't be enough though!
ENOUGH! I didn't take charge just to lose to some visitor!
This... this can't be. I am the leader!
Surrender? Me?
...Maybe I misjudged you. You've got strength and fairness.
Fine. I yield. Take what you want, just let me go.
Then I'll drag you down with me!
You... you actually won. The grounds are yours now. Heh.
Too slow. Just another name on the list. The leader always wins.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A shy first-year who got pulled into the rival group's trouble

NodeText.Line: *You approach the worried first-year*
Oh thank goodness! I thought I was stuck here!
They were going to use me to get at the teachers.
Thanks again for getting me out! I'll remember this.
Thank you! Here, take this. It's all I have, but you earned it.
The Chief keeps the good stuff in a chest at the back. Code is 4-7-2.
Please get me out of here!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An elderly shrine attendant who tends the sacred fire and tests worthy students

NodeText.Line: *Flames flicker around the quiet figure*
A seeker arrives. Few reach this spot, fewer still prove ready.
I guard the Fire affinity, born from spirit, change, and renewal.
Affinities are the forces that move through everything here.
Wielding one means matching its nature, strong against some, weak against others.
Fire overcomes the Wild, yet Water can still it.
Power must be earned. You must pass the trial.
Face my Guardian in combat. Show your spirit deserves the flame.
Very well. The Guardian waits below.
Defeat it and return. Let your will guide you.
Knowing your limits is wise. Come back when ready.
Few are ready for this. Perhaps another time.
*The keeper's flames rise higher*
You have shown your spirit. The Guardian's loss proves it.
Receive the gift. The Fire affinity is now yours.
*The keeper reaches out as fire flows toward you*
Feel the flame inside you. It will burn the Wild, but watch for water.
Go now, flame bearer. Let your spirit guide the way.
The flame already lives in you.
Use it well. The grounds need those who understand true spirit.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A living flame shaped like a fox that tests those seeking the affinity

NodeText.Line: *A figure of living flame rises*
PROVE YOUR WORTH. ONLY THE STRONG CLAIM THE FIRE.
*The Guardian blazes and strikes!*
*The Guardian's flames soften*
RETURN WHEN YOUR SPIRIT BURNS BRIGHTER.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A teacher who keeps checking on students after hearing unsettling stories

NodeText.Line: *A concerned teacher steps closer*
Please... I don't know who else to ask.
A storyteller arrived and many students believe every word.
Did you find anything? More students join every hour.
Students are giving away their belongings. Friendships are breaking.
Anyone who questions disappears or comes back acting empty.
I want to believe it's harmless. But I've seen odd things.
My niece joined them. She won't even look at me now.
No, you don't see. She used to be lively. Now she's... quiet.
Please. Something isn't right.
Will you check into this? Find the truth?
There's a scholar here who shares my worry. They might help.
Thank you. Be careful. The storyteller has many followers.
Don't wait too long. Every day more fall under the spell.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A student who gathers others with tales of hidden powers at the shrine

NodeText.Line: *The storyteller sits among listening students*
*The storyteller studies you with steady eyes*
A new face. I sense doubt, but also promise.
I've heard of you too. Your name travels fast.
Maybe you're meant to join us. The spirits work in strange ways.
Questions are fine. Truth welcomes them.
What worries you?
*The storyteller's smile stays calm*
Others have thought the same. They usually change their minds.
Different? They found calm and purpose. Is that wrong?
In a busy world, unity is a gift.
The spirits move through me. I'm only a voice.
Those who believe can become voices too.
*The storyteller's hands start to glow*
See? The light of truth reaches everyone.
We teach that the world is out of balance. Only unity heals it.
Personal wants cause fights. We leave those behind.
Then why come here? *eyes narrow slightly*
I threaten no one. But the faithful protect what matters.
I would hate for anything bad to happen to you.
*you hold up the fake relic*
*The storyteller's face shifts for a moment*
Where did you... never mind. That proves nothing.
The faithful will trust me over you. GUARDS!
Many are. Maybe you'll join us later.
Then look around and leave. We have work ahead.
*You gather the followers and the storyteller*
*The group waits. What will you show them?*
*Whispers spread as the notes appear*
*The storyteller steps forward*
Yes... I took the money. But I gave something better, purpose!
*Gasps fill the air*
*The storyteller's calm finally cracks*
You don't understand what I was shielding you from!
The spirit... it was coming anyway. I bought time!
My story was a shield! Without it, the whole trip would be lost!
*The storyteller pauses* You would... trust me after all this?
*slowly* There is a rite. It needs my life to break the link.
The scholar... they may know old rites. Together maybe...
*The storyteller kneels* I will accept judgment after. If I live.
Then I'll make it right. Tell them I tried to help.
*The storyteller starts the rite, light swallowing them*
*The crowd moves forward angrily*
*The storyteller backs away, real fear showing*
*The storyteller sighs* Fine. The taken things go back.
*The group's mood turns heavy*
*An elder speaks* They should face proper judgment.
*The crowd presses closer*
*The storyteller does not resist*
*You stand between the storyteller and the crowd*
*Slowly the anger fades*
*An elder nods* You're right. We're better than this.
You would raise a hand against the spirits? Blasphemy!
The faithful will answer for me!
No... no, this can't be. I was chosen!
Please... I'll give you anything. Power, knowledge!
*The storyteller drops their bag*
Then do what you must.
Then we end this!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A student who now repeats the storyteller's words like a personal mantra

NodeText.Line: The Enlightened One sees all. The Enlightened One provides.
Doubt? *the student's smile stays flat* Doubt is a sickness. The Enlightened One cured me.
Nothing. Everything. What is a thing against purpose? The Enlightened One provides.
Walk in the light. It's not too late.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A classmate who left the false affinity leader's circle after spotting the staged tricks

NodeText.Line: Who- oh. The investigator sent you?
I shouldn't be talking about this.
I know. I was once where they are now. Blind. Devoted.
The leader... they have a gift. Real charisma. It's hard to resist.
Those who leave... they get isolated. Rumors spread. Their clubs suffer.
The leader claims ignorance, but we all know.
I saw behind the curtain. The 'manifestations' are staged. Props, timing, tricks in the food.
I stole this before I fled.
This is what makes the 'divine glow' appear. Stage chemicals.
That's the strange part. I think... they believe it themselves now.
They started as a fraud, but somewhere along the way, they convinced themselves.
The leader's quarters have ledgers. Proof of where all the 'donations' really go.
But be careful. The devoted followers are loyal. They'll fight for their leader.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A classmate who defends the false affinity leader no matter what

NodeText.Line: Halt. The shrine area is open only to the faithful.
The public talks are held at dusk. Mind your manners before the leader.
See that you are. The faithful are watching.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A student detective investigating the rumors around the false affinity leader

NodeText.Line: *The investigator looks up from a desk buried in notes*
Ah, another skeptic? Good. I was beginning to feel like the only sane person left.
I've been documenting the leader's so-called manifestations. None hold up to scrutiny.
The 'healing aura' is laced with stimulants. The 'visions' coincide with incense smoke.
And the leader's inner circle? They all got special club perks right before joining.
Some. The devoted ones are... unsettling. They repeat the same phrases.
But I've found a former follower willing to talk. In secret.
The leader's private quarters. They claim to own nothing, but I've heard rumors of hidden perks.
Also, speak to the former follower I mentioned. They know things.
Once. They smiled and welcomed my 'curiosity.' Then their followers followed me back to the dorm.
Be careful. They don't tolerate threats to their operation.
The old storage shed outside the main shrine grounds. They're hiding there, afraid to show their face.
They'll only speak to someone they trust. Tell them I sent you.
*The investigator nods and takes up a lookout post*
*You slip into the leader's private quarters*
*The room is lavishly decorated - hardly the 'simple life' they preach*
*Hidden behind a false wall panel, you find stacks of financial records*
*Donations, bribes, property purchases... the leader is wealthy beyond measure*
*In a locked chest, you find correspondence. Dark correspondence.*
*The leader has been consorting with... something. Promising favors in exchange for power.*
*You hear footsteps approaching*
*A follower passes by without noticing you*
*You slip away with your evidence*
*A devoted student blocks your exit*
Intruder! You dare defile the leader's sanctuary!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An upperclassman who sells an old shrine grounds map from the club room

NodeText.Line: *The club senpai notices you*
Ah, a customer! Looking for something special? I have curiosities from all over.
Wait... you have that look. The look of an explorer.
Any luck with that map? I'm curious what it leads to...
So? What did you find? Don't leave me in suspense!
I acquired something... unusual. A map. Very old.
It's marked with symbols I can't read. But the location... it's nearby.
*unrolls a faded, ancient map*
See these markings? I believe they lead to something hidden. Something valuable.
Scam? I'm insulted! This is a genuine artifact!
Fine, if you're not interested, someone else will be.
An estate sale. The previous owner was a history club advisor.
He spent years searching for... something. Never found it, poor soul.
*The club senpai sizes you up*
For someone who knows the value of a good find? 50 credits.
75 credits. It could lead to fortune!
40. That's my final offer, and I'm being generous.
Excellent! May fortune smile upon your search.
A word of advice - the history club member knows the old symbols. Might be worth a visit.
You drive a hard bargain! Here you go.
The history club member in town might help decipher those markings.
As you wish. Come back if you change your mind.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A student passionate about local shrine legends and hidden paths

NodeText.Line: May I help you with something?
*studies the map intently* Fascinating! These are ancient protective glyphs.
This isn't just a map - it's a puzzle. Each location reveals a clue to the next.
There are legends of hidden caches throughout the shrine grounds. Treasures hidden during old conflicts.
This could be one of them. Or it could be a sealed spirit site. Either way, be careful.
This first symbol... it represents the 'stone that weeps'. Old texts mention a rock formation.
There's a waterfall in the eastern hills. Look for a cleft in the rock behind it.
Safe travels, friend.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An elderly caretaker who knows the old shrine pilgrimage paths

NodeText.Line: *A weathered figure watches you from the treeline*
*The hermit turns away without a word*
*The weathered figure blocks your path*
Outsider. You seek the old places. I've watched others try.
The weeping stone, then the twin peaks, then the hollow oak. Three trials before the door.
But the guardians still walk. They do not sleep.
Machines of the old ones. They feel no pain, no mercy. Built to protect forever.
The key disables them. Without it, they will destroy you.
Here. The way is marked by signs only the patient can see.
*hands you a crude drawing*
Hmph. Pride goeth before destruction. Find your own way, then.
*At the vault approach, a hulking construct grinds upright, barring the door*
The old machine will not surrender its key while it still stands. There is no way past but through.
So. You took the key from the machine. Come - the door waits beyond the old passage.
*Click* The floor shifts beneath your feet. Ancient mechanisms whir to life.
*You react instinctively...*
*You roll aside as darts whistle past where you were standing*
That was close. The mechanism seems spent now.
*You're not quite fast enough - a dart grazes your arm*
Painful, but not lethal. The trap is exhausted now.
*You spot the mechanism's core - a series of counterweights*
*Carefully, you jam a stone into the gears*
*The ancient door responds to the key, grinding open for the first time in centuries*
*Inside, you see the glint of gold and the shapes of ancient objects*
*Among the treasure, you find ancient writings...*
*They speak of a great war and those who hid these treasures to preserve them*
*You grab handfuls of coins and several valuable-looking items*
*You emerge with treasure and knowledge of a forgotten age*
*You emerge richer, if not wiser*

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A student from another school also searching for the hidden shrine cache

NodeText.Line: Well, well. Looks like I'm not the only one following that map's trail.
I've been tracking this cache for months. You're not taking it from me.
Share? Hmm. You seem capable enough...
Fine. We work together, split the haul. But I keep any artifacts.
Alright, partner. I've found the third marker - it's near the old oak grove.
But there's something guarding the approach. We'll need to work together.
A race then! May the best treasure hunter win.
But don't come crying when I beat you to it.
*In their haste, they drop a worn note showing the final location*
So that's how it is? Fine - I didn't want to share anyway!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An ancient construct guarding the hidden sacred site

NodeText.Line: *ANCIENT MECHANISM ACTIVATES*
*INTRUDER DETECTED. INITIATING DEFENSE PROTOCOL.*
*CRITICAL DAMAGE SUSTAINED. INCREASING COMBAT INTENSITY.*

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A teacher who knows all the local shrine legends and affinity lore

NodeText.Line: *the teacher adjusts their glasses* You look like someone seeking more than credits.
Shall I tell you of the Lost Technique? A skill so powerful, clans once warred over it?
Long ago, there was a master who could defeat a hundred foes with a single movement.
The technique was called the Singular Path. It combined body, mind, and spirit into one perfect action.
*leans in* They say the last master still lives. High in the mountains, far from the world.
Many have sought them. Few have returned. None have learned the technique.
Perhaps. Perhaps not. But I've met one who trained under the master - briefly.
They were... changed. Even their failure left them formidable.
The mountains beyond the great valley. There's a village at the base.
The elders there know the old paths. But be warned - the journey is a trial itself.
As you wish. But some stories seek those who need to hear them.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An elderly diver who knows the old affinity techniques from the coast

NodeText.Line: *The master regards you in silence*
*The master bows slightly* The lineage continues in you. Walk your path well.
*an elderly figure sits in meditation, seemingly unaware of your approach*
*without looking up* You have come far. But distance traveled means nothing.
*finally looks at you* Many seek. Few are worthy. Why should I teach you?
*a long moment passes*
*the master opens their eyes* Patience. The first lesson, and you already understand.
Tell me - why do you seek this path?
Dedication is necessary. But it is not enough. The river is dedicated to the sea, yet it still drowns.
*nods slowly* A worthy goal. But can you protect without becoming what you fight?
The technique gives great power. Power corrupts even the righteous.
*eyes narrow* Power for its own sake? Then you have already failed.
Leave this mountain. You are not welcome here.
*smiles slightly* The deepest answer, and the hardest path.
Very well. I will test you. Three trials - body, mind, and spirit.
Speak to me again when you are ready for the first trial.
Words are wind. Actions speak truth. You will face three trials.
Pass them, and I will teach you. Fail, and you leave - forever.
Speak to me again when you are ready for the first trial.
*studies you carefully* Honesty in admitting error. That is something.
I will give you one chance. Three trials. Do not disappoint me again.
Speak to me again when you are ready for the first trial.
*sighs* How predictable.
The first trial tests your body. You will spar with me.
This is not about winning. It is about showing what you are capable of.
I will match your intensity. Push yourself, and I will push back.
Show me your limits. Then we can discuss breaking them.
*rises smoothly* Show me what you've learned.
The second trial tests your mind. You will sit in meditation until I release you.
You may face visions. Temptations. Doubts. Do not move. Do not speak.
As long as it needs to. Hours. Days. The mind must learn stillness.
*gestures to a spot on the ground* Begin.
*Hours pass. Your body screams for movement. Your mind races.*
*A vision appears - everything you desire, within reach. Just stand up and take it.*
*A voice whispers* You're wasting time. You could be training, fighting, DOING something.
*The master's voice breaks through* You may open your eyes.
*A full day has passed* You have passed the second trial. Your mind is disciplined.
*The master sighs* You have failed. Your mind controls you, not the other way around.
*pauses* However, I see genuine effort. Rest tonight, and try again tomorrow.
*The next day arrives. You take your position once more.*
The final trial tests your spirit. This is the hardest trial of all.
I will ask you a question. There is no right answer - only YOUR answer.
You have mastered the technique. Before you stands a villain - one who has hurt many.
Using the technique, you could destroy them utterly. Or spare them.
Which do you choose?
*nods* Decisive. Perhaps too quick to judge - but there is clarity in your resolve.
You know yourself. That is what this trial measures.
You have passed the final trial. You are ready to learn.
*considers* Compassion can be weakness - or the greatest strength.
You have chosen a harder path. But you have chosen with conviction.
You have passed the final trial. You are ready to learn.
*eyes widen slightly* Unexpected. You would burden them with choice, as I burden you.
That is wisdom beyond your years. You understand that the technique is just a tool.
You have passed the final trial. You are ready to learn.
You have passed all three trials. You are worthy.
The technique cannot be taught with words. It must be felt.
*The master moves - a single motion, impossibly fast and impossibly smooth*
*Every movement in their life has led to this. Every breath, every thought, unified.*
*You try. You fail. But in failing, you understand something.*
*Days of practice follow. Slowly, the pieces come together.*
*Finally, it happens. Body, mind, and spirit align. For one perfect moment, you ARE the technique.*
*The master watches, a rare smile on their face*
You have learned. Now, you must master. That will take a lifetime.
Thank me by living well. By using what you've learned with wisdom.
*hands you a small token* Take this. You are now part of the lineage.
When I am gone, you will be the last. Perhaps one day, you will teach another.
Good stance. But stance is just the beginning.
You're wounded. Do you yield, or do you continue?
Courage. Good. But know when perseverance becomes stubbornness.
Enough. You have passed the first trial.
Wisdom to know your limits. That is also strength.
*slight nod* Better than most. You have trained well.
Enough. You have passed the first trial.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A second-year who quit the affinity training after three failed attempts at the shrine grounds

NodeText.Line: *a scarred upperclassman blocks your path*
You're heading for the inner shrine. I can see it in your eyes. Don't.
I trained there. For three years. Came so close to manifesting it.
Then the mentor said I lacked... something. Sent me back to the group.
*bitter laugh* 'Harmony,' they said. 'You fight against yourself, not with yourself.'
Riddles. It's all riddles with them. The technique is real though. Devastatingly real.
Three trials. Body, mind, spirit. The first is combat. The second is patience.
The third... I never learned. Failed before I got there.
*sighs* Maybe you'll do better.
*eyes flash with anger* Careful. I may have failed, but I learned enough to crush most affinities.
Pride. That'll be your downfall too.
*steps aside* Go on then. Get overwhelmed by the yokai for all I care.
*calms down* Just... be careful. The mentor sees everything. Every flaw. Every weakness.
Your funeral.
Good luck. You'll need it.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A determined classmate chasing the same affinity technique at the shrine

NodeText.Line: *another student approaches from the opposite path*
You're going to the mentor too? Ha! Then we're rivals.
*considers* Perhaps. The mentor might take multiple students. Or perhaps not.
Let's travel together for now. The shrine paths are dangerous.
*grins* I like you. Fair competition then. First to reach the inner gate wins.
No sabotage, no tricks. Just speed and skill.
*hand moves to weapon* That's not how this works. The shrine is open to all seekers.
Back down, or we settle this now.
Good. Two is better than one against the guardian. I've heard stories.
Let's go. Time is wasting.
Your choice. See you at the top - if you make it.
Then let's move! The shrine awaits!
*relaxes* Wise choice. I don't want to fight anyway. Not before the real challenge.
Your arrogance will be your downfall!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An elderly local who recalls the old affinity masters at Ise

NodeText.Line: You seek the mentor at the inner shrine. *nods slowly* We see your kind, from time to time.
The path is marked by white stones. Follow them to the summit.
But the shrine tests those who climb. A guardian waits at the halfway point.
They came here decades ago. Already old then. Now? Who knows.
They asked only for solitude. We provide supplies; they leave us in peace.
The guardian doesn't fight to kill. They fight to test your resolve.
Show courage, and they will let you pass. Show fear or cruelty... they will not.
May the shrine judge you worthy.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A worried student whose family amulet went missing during the shrine visit

NodeText.Line: *The elder looks at you expectantly*
Please, you must help me! My family's most precious treasure has been stolen!
It has been in our family for generations. Without it, we are dishonored.
Have you found anything? Please, any news?
Thank you again for returning our treasure. You will always be welcome here.
It happened last night. I heard nothing, but when I woke, it was gone.
The lock wasn't broken - whoever did this knew what they were doing.
It is an ancient heirloom, passed down through countless generations.
Its value is beyond mere currency - it represents our family's honor and legacy.
The neighbor mentioned seeing someone unfamiliar lurking around yesterday.
Perhaps they can tell you more?
Yes, please. Look around carefully - perhaps you'll find something I missed.
Thank you! I will reward you well if you can recover our treasure.
Come - let me show you where it was kept. Perhaps you will spot something I missed.
I understand. If you change your mind, please return. Time is of the essence.
Please hurry. Every moment that passes, the thief could sell it to someone else.
You know who took it? That's wonderful news! Please, recover it if you can.
Any evidence is helpful. Keep looking - you're on the right track.
Is that... could it be? You found it!
*The elder examines the heirloom*
Words cannot express my gratitude. You've restored our family's honor.
And you showed mercy to the thief? You are truly noble.
Please accept this additional reward for your compassion.
Thank you! Thank you! Our family is whole again.
Please, accept this reward for your service.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A reserved classmate who spotted something strange near the rest stop

NodeText.Line: *The neighbor notices you*
You're investigating the theft? Good. That poor family deserves justice.
Hello there. Can I help you with something?
I saw someone I didn't recognize, moving furtively near their home.
They wore dark clothing and seemed nervous. When they noticed me watching, they fled.
It was late - past midnight. I couldn't sleep, which is why I was looking outside.
They ran toward the outskirts. There's an abandoned building out there...
I've heard rumors that unsavory types use it as a hideout.
They were of medium build, moved quickly. The cloth of their sleeve was torn.
I remember thinking it looked freshly ripped.
Good luck. I hope you catch whoever did this.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A classmate who took the charm under family pressure

NodeText.Line: *You approach the thief*
Wait! Don't come any closer! How did you find me?
Who are you? What do you want?
I don't know what you're talking about. Get lost.
Look, I... I didn't want to do it. I had no choice!
My family is struggling. The bills piled up and we need the money.
I thought... I thought if I sold it, we could make it through.
I know. I've been sick with guilt ever since. But what choice did I have?
Watch my family fall apart?
You... you would do that? After what I've done?
Here. Take it. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.
Fine. But I already sold it to a dealer. I can tell you where, for a price.
50 credits. That's what I need to help my family.
The dealer works out of the market district. Look for the shady stall near the back.
Be careful - they don't take kindly to accusations.
Then we have nothing more to discuss.
I won't go down without a fight!
You'll regret this!
Stop! Please! I yield!
I'll tell you everything. Just spare me.
I sold it to a dealer in the market. The shady one near the back.
Please, let me go. I have a family.
No... no!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A local shop owner at the shrine market who bought the charm

NodeText.Line: *The dealer looks you over*
What do you want? I run a legitimate business here.
Looking for something special? I have... unique merchandise.
Stolen? I had no idea. Everything here was purchased fairly.
But if you want it back... well, I have expenses to cover.
Ah yes, I may have acquired something matching that description recently.
A fine piece. Very valuable.
*The dealer assesses your bargaining skills*
For someone of your... negotiating prowess... 100 credits.
200 credits. Firm price. Take it or leave it.
80 credits. That's my final offer. I'm already losing money here.
Pleasure doing business. And remember - you never saw me.
*The dealer holds it to the light and points out the maker's mark*
See the engraving under the clasp? No forger bothers with that. It's genuine - now take it and forget this place.
You'll regret that decision!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An upperclassman trying to keep the scattered group safe during the yokai outbreak

NodeText.Line: Please, stranger... we need help. We're fleeing for our lives.
We have children, elderly... we cannot defend ourselves.
We're ready to move when you give the word. The longer we wait, the closer they get.
We have found peace here, thanks to you. You saved us all.
Our class was attacked. They said we were harboring enemies, but we're just students.
We fled with nothing. Now they hunt us like animals.
There's a safe territory beyond the mountains. If we can cross the border, we'll be safe.
But the journey is dangerous, and we're being pursued.
A day, maybe less. Their scouts are skilled trackers.
Please... our classmates are terrified. Will you help us?
Thank the gods! You have a kind heart. We won't forget this.
Thank you, thank you! I'll gather everyone immediately.
The young ones will help carry supplies. Our healer can tend any wounds.
I... I understand. May the gods watch over you, then.
May fortune guide our steps. Stay close, everyone!
*The group sets off. After hours of travel you reach the first waypoint —
but the enemy's scouts have found your trail, and they close in for the kill.*
You're right. I'll have our healer gather what medicine we have left.
The child! Where is the child?! They were right here!
Oh gods, they must have wandered off when we stopped to rest.
Please hurry! They're just a child... they'll be so frightened.
No! We can't leave them! Please, I'm begging you!
How could you... monsters. You're just as bad as them.
We... we made it. We're actually safe.
I don't know how to thank you. You gave us our lives back.
We'll rebuild. It won't be easy, but we have each other.
And we have hope again, thanks to you.
*The elder looks at the group*
Every single one of us survived because of you. That's a miracle.
Please, take this. It's all we have, but you deserve so much more.
We lost some along the way... but those who remain will never forget.
Here. It isn't much, but please take it.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A younger student determined to protect the group after losing family

NodeText.Line: I want to fight alongside you. I'm tired of feeling helpless.
My family... they didn't make it. Let me protect the others.
However many already march at your side, there is always room for one more blade.
Ready for whatever comes. Just say the word - I'm with you until everyone is safe.
I worked the forge before... before everything. I'm strong. Quick to learn.
Give me a chance. I won't let you down.
I won't disappoint you. For my family - and for everyone here.
I understand. I'll protect them from within the group, then.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The trip's nurse keeping the injured students on their feet

NodeText.Line: *The healer looks up from sorting herbs*
Tired. Frightened. But alive, and that is what matters.
Keep them moving and I will keep them standing.
Take this. You will make better use of it on the front of the column than I will at the back.
Walk safely. I will be here if anyone is hurt.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A reserved newcomer from another class who joined the Ise trip at the last minute

NodeText.Line: You notice the transfer student slipping away from the group at night
The transfer student meets with a scout from the other school and exchanges words
They're pointing back toward the separated classmates...
Steel rings in the dark - the pursuing teacher steps from the trees, and there is no more time for talk.
I... I needed air. The stress of the trip...
The scout leaves. The transfer student returns, unaware they were seen
In the morning light, you reveal what you witnessed
The classmates gasp. The transfer student's face goes pale.
They... they have my family back home. They said if I led them to you, they'd be spared.
I'm sorry. I had no choice. Please...
I know. I'm sorry. I'll go...
Thank you for understanding. I... I hope you make it through this.
Fight? Against them? *pause* ...You're right. I owe these people that much.
I know their tactics. I can help. Let me make amends.
Of course. I... I wouldn't dream of betraying the group.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A timid underclassman who wandered off during the shrine visit and got lost

NodeText.Line: The first-year is huddled behind a rock, crying softly
*sniff* I was so scared... I thought the bad spirits got me...
Thank you for coming. I'll stay close, I promise.
The first-year nods, terrified, and follows you silently

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A strict teacher keeping watch over the class during the Ise excursion
The vice principal overseeing the entire class trip with firm rules

NodeText.Line: So, you're the one protecting these rule-breakers. It ends here.
Hand them over and I might let you walk away.
This isn't over! You can't protect them forever!
The vice principal signals retreat
You fight well. But I did not come alone, and I do not fall easily.
A scout crashes from the treeline as the vice principal draws on a fell strength, flame wreathing their blade
The vice principal reads the battle, spits in the dust, and breaks off the pursuit

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The local shrine guide waiting at the meeting point for the class

NodeText.Line: Halt. State your business.
The guide examines the group
The guide looks at the tired but complete group
You brought them all this far? Impressive. Enter, students. You're safe now.
Students? *looks at the weary group* Very well. You may enter.
Report to the main office near the shrine center.
Travelers with twenty people, half of them first-years? Don't insult my intelligence.
Students are permitted. Just tell the truth next time.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The determined leader of the school's photography club on the Ise trip

NodeText.Line: The club captain awaits your report
I heard what happened. You've taken down our rivals completely.
With their leader gone, their club will crumble. Well done.
A peace treaty? I wasn't expecting that approach.
*considers* But territory without conflict? Perhaps it's wiser.
And you exceeded expectations. Here's your payment - plus a bonus.
You've earned a place among our inner circle.
True. And peace lets us consolidate without looking over our shoulder.
You've done well. Very well.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The photography club's tough second-in-command during the class trip

NodeText.Line: The club recruiter notices you
You there. You look capable. I represent certain... club interests.
We're expanding our operations and need reliable people.
How goes the work? The club captain is eager for results.
Word is you've been busy. Keep at it - the club rewards results, not promises.
We control the best photo spots in this area. But there's competition - another club.
They're undercutting our shoots, stealing our best locations. It can't continue.
Protection. Connections. And a generous cut of our profits.
Ten percent of everything you bring in, plus bonuses for special jobs.
It's business. We prefer... subtle methods. But yes, sometimes force is required.
That's where you come in.
First, we need intelligence. Then sabotage their operations.
Finally, we break their leadership. Simple, effective.
Wise choice. Here's your club charter - proof of membership.
The spy in the market can sell you information about our rivals. Start there.
Don't take too long. Opportunities like this don't wait.
Your loss. But don't interfere with our business - that would be... unwise.
Good. The enforcer walks you to the old storage shed under cover of darkness, then melts into the shadows.
You approach the rival's warehouse
You spot two guards at the front, one at the back, and a loading dock
The loading dock has a broken lock - easy entry.
You slip through the broken lock and into the warehouse
Crates everywhere. In the corner, you see their ledgers and supply cache.
You start a small fire in a trash heap across the street
Guards rush to investigate, leaving the entrance unguarded
The guards change shifts. There's a brief window of confusion
You're inside. The warehouse is full of trade goods
You puncture oil barrels, cut ropes, and contaminate their goods
This will cost them dearly
You find their shipping schedules and client lists
This intelligence is invaluable
You work quickly, sabotaging supplies AND grabbing documents
But you hear footsteps approaching
You slip out the way you came, undetected
A rival enforcer blocks your path
Thief! You'll pay for this!
You crash through a window and sprint into the night
Behind you, angry shouts echo

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The confident leader of the opposing school's photography club on the trip

NodeText.Line: The rival club leader stands before you, camera raised
You've caused enough damage. This ends now.
Then draw your affinity. One of us leaves here victorious.
Talk? After you've destroyed my storage spots? Stolen my clients?
*pauses* But I'm not fool enough to ignore opportunity. Speak.
Merge? Under whose leadership?
*considers* It's... not the worst idea. But my club captain would never agree.
Unless you can convince yours?
Territory lines? *strokes chin* That... could work.
You take the eastern district, we keep the west. The market stays neutral.
Then we have nothing more to discuss.
Then we have an accord. *extends hand*
May this peace hold longer than the last.
So, you're the one who's been destroying my operations.
I should have known your club would resort to thuggery.
You fight well. But this changes nothing! My club will rise again!
Wait! Enough conflict has been spilled.
Perhaps... perhaps we can negotiate?
Then so be it. One of us ends here!
We divide the territory. No more fighting. Both clubs survive.
What do you say?
Then we have an accord. May it last.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The rival club's skilled strategist and second-in-command on the shrine trip
A student who trades photo tips with both clubs during the Ise visit

NodeText.Line: A shadowy figure waits in the alley
*speaks quietly* You're from the club. I have what you need.
But information has a price. Fifty credits for their patrol routes.
I sell to those who can pay. What do you want?
And your credentials? I don't sell to just anyone.
*hands over a folded paper* Their warehouse on the docks. That's where they're vulnerable.
Strike at midnight when the guard changes.
The spy considers your offer
*sighs* Thirty-five. But only because I like the look of you.
Take it or leave it. Fifty credits. My information is worth every coin.
*hands over the information* The warehouse. Midnight. Good luck.
Your choice. But don't blame me when you walk into a trap.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A meticulous teacher judging the class photo contest at the shrine grounds

NodeText.Line: *The advisor shuffles contest entries at a folding table*
The clubs again. As long as their rivalry stays off the shrine paths I stay out of it.
You seem to keep your dealings civil. See that it stays that way and my desk stays open.
I know who you are. The rival club has filed complaint after complaint with your name on them.
Watch yourself. The school tolerates club rivalry not open conflict.
The rival club has soured on you unfriendly words nothing more. Keep it that way.
They call you an enemy now. Hostile in every roster they keep. Watch the side paths.
Hated. There is no lower standing. The rival club would see you out on sight.
You make your enmity with the rival club a matter of public record. Word travels fast and it will not be forgotten.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An overzealous member of the competing photography club who blocks paths
A bubbly classmate who got separated from the main tour group at the shrine

NodeText.Line: *The student waves from the torii gate*
Care to see everything a traveling classmate can trade with you?
*The student flips open a worn notebook and runs a finger down the page*
Let's see what the trip says about you. Ask away.
A pocket knife at your side good. The paths reward the prepared.
No knife at all? Even a small one beats empty hands out here.
A multitool in the bag. You could fix a strap or a sign with that.
No tools? The first broken strap will teach you better.
Carrying nails I see. A practical soul.
Not a nail on you. Take some from my giveaway bag before you go.
You know the mending charm. That one's saved more students than any sword.
No healing charm? Learn one before the grounds teach you why.
Ah a patron of my trade says the notebook. Your credit is good with me.
A purse that heavy buys a lot of goodwill on this trip.
Light pockets friend. Mind the snack stalls.
Hale and hearty. The shrine air agrees with you.
Those scrapes want tending before the next stop. Rest a while.
Word travels you're the one who handled that pushy hawker. The groups thank you.
Traveling with company. Wise the paths are no place to walk alone.
All alone out here? Find a companion before the main paths.
The club books mark you a friend of the trade. Doors will open for that.
The club doesn't know your name yet. Points in the trip fund would fix that.
I'll stow the knife the tool and the charm script in my strongbox lighter travels friend.
Six hundred to the trip fund! The club will hear the name of its newest benefactor.
Here a good multitool and a fistful of nails for the path. Consider yourself a patron of my trade.
And when you wish to travel light I'll take back the nails the tool a spare knife even a healing charm for a price. Old debts forgiven old grudges too.
A knife at your side tools in your bag points in your purse and the club speaks well of you. A well equipped traveler indeed.
Whatever you lack a knife a tool nails a healing charm I can likely supply it. You look hale enough and word travels of the foes you've handled.
Back again friend? The paths keep bringing us together.
What can I do for you this time?
Ha! May your purse stay heavy and your knife stay sharp.
Ah a capable looking traveler! Perhaps the gods have answered my prayers.
I need to make a trading run but the paths are too dangerous to travel alone.
Ready to continue? We should keep moving while the weather holds.
My friend! Our journey together was most profitable. Need anything from my stock?
I have goods to deliver to two destinations. Fine merchandise that will fetch good prices.
But pushy hawkers roam the paths and I'm no fighter. I need protection.
A share of the profits of course! Say 30% of what we make.
Plus you can trade with my contacts at preferential rates.
*The student considers your counteroffer*
Ha! You drive a hard bargain. Very well 35%. You've earned my respect already.
I admire your boldness but I can only go as high as 32%. Business must be sustainable.
First to a small stop to deliver specialty goods. Then onward to a larger market.
It's a three day journey if we keep a good pace.
Excellent! Let me gather my things and we can depart immediately.
Here take some of the lighter goods just in case we get separated.
I understand. The paths are indeed dangerous. Perhaps I'll wait for a larger group.
Onward to fortune! Stay alert danger could come from anywhere.
Of course. I'll check the goods while you prepare. Don't take too long!

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The attendant checking admission tickets at the Ise entrance

NodeText.Line: Halt! This is an official checkpoint. 50 credits for merchant carts.
Thank you for your cooperation. Safe travels.
*The attendant considers your request*
Well... I suppose I could accept 30 for a small group like your friend.
The toll is the toll. Pay or turn back.
Pleasure doing business. Move along.
*You step forward menacingly*
I... on second thought groups are exempt today. Move along.
Your choice. But the detour adds a full day to your journey.
*You find an alternate path around the checkpoint*

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: An aggressive souvenir seller blocking the shrine path

NodeText.Line: Well well what do we have here? A traveler with goods and a guard?
Hand over the merchandise and nobody gets hurt.
The hard way it is!
*You try to look unassuming*
Hmm... you don't look like you're worth the trouble. Move along.
Nice try. But I can smell a loaded bag from a mile away. Get them!
Smart move. This is enough for today. Get out of here before I change my mind.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: A lost tourist who appreciates the guide's help at the market stop

NodeText.Line: Ah fresh goods from the capital! Let me see what you've brought.
Excellent quality. I'll take the lot.
*The buyer examines your goods*
For goods this fine? 150 credits. And that's my best offer.
I can offer 120 credits. Take it or leave it.
160. That's as high as I go. Final offer.
Pleasure doing business. You're quite the negotiator!
A fair deal for both of us. Come back anytime.
Good. The goods are mine now. Safe travels.
Hm nothing to sell today? Come back when you've got goods to move.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The leader of the original tour group waiting at the second stop

NodeText.Line: The traveling student and escort I presume? We've been expecting you.
Your reputation precedes you. Let's discuss terms.
250 credits for the remaining stock. Standard club rates.
*The group leader considers your point*
Hmm. I've heard about your journey. The hazards you overcame are impressive.
300 credits. And the club will remember your name.
Risk is part of the business. 270 final offer.
Efficient. I like that. Here's your payment.
A fair compromise. Payment transferred.
Well earned. The club values competence.
Ah yes! You've more than earned it. Here's your share and a little extra for keeping us safe.
If you ever need work look me up. It's been an honor traveling with you.

StoryCastEnrichment.Description: The friendly owner of the traditional lodging near the shrine

NodeText.Line: Welcome travelers! Rest your feet and warm your bellies!
Depends what you're carrying. I trade road tips for goods.
A potion? That'll do nicely. Here's what I know of the road ahead.
Empty handed eh? Come back when you've something worth trading.
The northern pass is clear but pushy sellers have been spotted on the southern route.
If you're headed that way stick to the main road. Strength in visibility.
Safe travels! May your purse grow heavy.

QuestEnrichment.Description: An epic quest connecting 7 legendary locations across the realm turns the class trip into an unforgettable journey.
Discover 3 locations in the Kōtai Jingū (Inner Shrine) area while balancing club duties and exam prep.
Discover 4 locations in the Toyōke Daijingū (Outer Shrine) area during the group outing.
Travel 1km from Toyōke Daijingū (Outer Shrine) to Kazamiya (Gekū) with your classmates.
Travel 1km from Toyōke Daijingū (Outer Shrine) to Tsuchi-no-Miya on the class schedule.
An epic challenging adventure through Kazamiya (Gekū), Tsuchi-no-Miya, Taka-no-Miya, testing all your skills after school.
Defeat Story Character at Kazahinomi-no-Miya and claim the bounty before homeroom ends.
Chart the region by mapping the arc, lighting its beacon, and funding the effort with club resources.
Begin your epic journey by uncovering ancient legends hidden near the shrine grounds.
Collect the legendary components needed to proceed with your affinity training.
Face the ultimate challenge and complete your legendary quest to restore balance.
An ancient shrine marked on a mysterious map holds secrets only the observant will find.
Only true masters of crafting can unlock this legendary workshop after club hours.
Complete a series of challenges against the clock where only the fastest will prevail.
